messages:
maya: heads-up — customer reported huge latency + intermittent 503s for requests that should be hitting eu-west. they see routing to na-west-2 instead. example req id: req_0a12b3. started ~09:45 UTC, impact on production tier. any quick triage?

josh: looking. initial glance at router logs shows eu-west pool hit soft capacity and autospillover kicked in, routing a subset to na-west-2. however a chunk of those requests then returned 401/403. suspect token region-scope mismatch during spillover.

luis: i pulled a sample trace for req_0a12b3 — here's the condensed flow:
```
2025-10-12T09:45:21Z router: incoming -> route pool=eu-west-1 (util=98%)
2025-10-12T09:45:23Z router: pool eu-west-1 soft_threshold exceeded -> spillover -> target=na-west-2
2025-10-12T09:45:24Z na-west-2 gateway: auth fail -> reason=token_scope_invalid region=eu-west-1
2025-10-12T09:45:24Z requester: 503 (after retry)
```

luis: note the na-west gateway rejects tokens that are scoped to eu-region-only keys. those should have been translated or retried with a fallback token but we don't have that mechanism for private keys.

katie: customer also flagged a billing spike — they were billed inter-region egress + additional tokens from retries when failing over. total tokens charged ~3x for some sessions. they want an immediate cost mitigation.

maya: repro steps i ran quickly:
1) set region header X-Region: eu-west-1
2) pump concurrent requests (~350) with very long seq lengths
3) observe router log: soft-spillover threshold at 95% local concurrency -> some requests routed out
4) requests routed out fail with 401 if the API key has region-scoped claims

example curl:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_eu_..." -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-qa","prompt":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

josh: quick mitigation suggestions:
- short term: add a routing rule to prefer local-only if token scope==region and return 425/429 instead of silent spillover. that avoids cross-region auth errors and unexpected billing.
- medium term: implement token translation/relay for autospillover so requests keep valid auth when moved across pools.
- customer fix: pin requests to eu-west via customer config (region_pin=true) or increase reserved capacity.

infra-bot: Autospillover alert: pool=eu-west-1, event=soft_capacity_exceeded, timestamp=2025-10-12T09:45:23Z, routed_count=412, fallback=na-west-2, policy=default_spillover

katie: customer asked for a root-cause writeup + invoice adjustment for cross-region egress and retry token charges. do we have telemetry to prove which requests were billed due to failover vs normal?

luis: yes — billing traces include route_id and billed_region. i can produce a slice by customer id and route_id, but need access to finance role to redact PII.

maya: can eng-runtime look at making spillover-auth-safe? immediate ask: disable silent cross-region spillover for region-scoped keys and return a clear 409/region_mismatch or 429 so customers can handle it. tagging eng-runtime now.

josh: agreed. i'll open a quick rollback PR to change default spillover behavior and add a canary flag. small patch: if token.scope == "region_only" -> route_policy = "reject_spillover".

katie: noted — i'll tell the customer we can prevent future surprise cross-region billing and that we're preparing a fix and offer a billing review.

maya: thanks all — assigning follow-ups: josh to PR/rollout, luis to produce billing slice, katie to customer comms. i'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
